subject: Trial procurement & conversion next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@omnihealth.com>, Chris Lane <chris.lane@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Trial procurement & conversion next steps

Hi Alex / Chris —

Great speaking with you this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery so we all have alignment: 

Summary of today's call
- Trial target: 3-week pilot of Redwood inference for OmniHealth analytics pipelines (approx. 2M tokens/week expected)
- Success criteria: 1) end-to-end inference latency within 150ms P50 on representative workload; 2) embedding similarity recall >= 92% on the validation set; 3) evidence of 2 production routes using the Redwood API by pilot end
- Billing trigger: trial will convert to paid when agreed usage threshold is reached OR on the start date we agree for billing (see options below)

Procurement / commercial path options we discussed
1) Purchase Order (PO) — OmniHealth can issue a PO to Redwood. We can accept Net30. We will provide a SOW and invoice once PO is in place.
2) Corporate card — for faster start, payment by card is possible (no PO required).
3) Cloud Marketplace — if you prefer procurement via the Azure marketplace, we can enable that, but there is a marketplace listing lead time and different billing cadence.

Action items / next steps
- Alex / Chris: confirm preferred procurement path (PO vs card vs marketplace) and internal billing contact (Chris?) — by EOD Thu 2/4
- Procurement: if PO, share required PO template and any additional paperwork we should include
- Marissa / Dev: we will share a short procurement checklist, a SOW draft, and the HubSpot/DocuSign links for signature and billing start options

Attachments I will follow up with: procurement-checklist.xlsx, SOW-draft.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call with procurement if useful.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123
https://redwood.ai
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@omnihealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Chris Lane <chris.lane@omnihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 11:05:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Trial procurement & conversion next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple quick items from our side:

- Procurement preference: PO (our standard process) — we generally do Net30.
- Billing contact: Chris Lane (cc'd) handles purchasing.
- Marketplace: we'd prefer direct PO for faster procurement; marketplace would introduce a month delay for procurement approvals.
- Billing start: we'd like the trial to be free during the 3-week pilot and have billing start on the agreed conversion date (we'll confirm exact date after we validate success criteria). If we exceed the usage threshold during trial, is there a mechanism to cap spend or pause?

Can you send the SOW and the procurement checklist for our legal/procurement review? Also please include a sample invoice template so finance knows the expected line items.

Regards,
Alex

Hi Chris / Procurement Team / Alex —

Thanks — attaching the SOW draft and procurement checklist we discussed. Couple clarifications inline below and answers to your questions: 

- Redwood legal name for PO: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Payment terms: Net30 (we can do Net45 for enterprise if requested — please flag)
- Billing trigger: by default we start billing on the agreed conversion date. If usage exceeds the agreed trial threshold before conversion, we can either 1) auto-convert early (with prior notice), or 2) cap token usage and pause further traffic. Please indicate your preferred approach — most customers choose to cap usage until a PO is issued.
- SOC2 / security: SOC2 Type II report and subprocessor list: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 and I've included a short summary in the SOW appendix.

- SOW-draft.pdf (stub)
